formats.text_frames: the exact UTF-8 text of a data-channel text frame
formats.binary_frames: hex of the whole wire frame (7-byte header + payload)
formats.large_binary_frames: base64 of the whole frame when longer than 512 bytes
formats.decoded: each frame carries its decoded meaning alongside

attach_control.summary: the "control" data-channel attach frame (the first text frame on the channel)
attach_control.outcome: answered by the attach ack; a resent frame (the ack was lost) is re-acknowledged with the same ack
attach_control.template: substitute a live controller_key from POST /api/v1/controller for <SESSION-KEY> to replay

attach_scope.summary: the "scope" data-channel attach frame (the first text frame on the channel)
attach_scope.outcome: answered by the attach ack; a resent frame (the ack was lost) is re-acknowledged with the same ack
attach_scope.template: substitute a live controller_key from POST /api/v1/controller for <SESSION-KEY> to replay

attach_audio.summary: the "audio" data-channel attach frame (the first text frame on the channel)
attach_audio.outcome: answered by the attach ack; a resent frame (the ack was lost) is re-acknowledged with the same ack
attach_audio.template: substitute a live controller_key from POST /api/v1/controller for <SESSION-KEY> to replay

attach_api.summary: the "api" data-channel attach frame (the first text frame on the channel)
attach_api.outcome: no ack and no hello: the channel stays silent until its first request (this is how a browser acquires its first key)

attach_ack_scope.summary: the scope attach ack (the first text frame the server sends)
attach_ack_scope.outcome: the client stops resending its attach; control and api channels never send one

attach_ack_audio.summary: the audio attach ack (the first text frame the server sends)
attach_ack_audio.outcome: the client stops resending its attach; control and api channels never send one

api_request_tx_refused.summary: an api request with a body: POST /api/v1/civ/transaction, id 1
api_request_tx_refused.outcome: one REQ_HEAD, body chunks (<= 16 KB each), then END; the body is transmit-capable, so the answer is api_response_tx_refused

api_response_tx_refused.summary: the 403 for a transmit-capable body, id 1
api_response_tx_refused.outcome: the shared dispatch is never reached: RES_HEAD 403, one RES_BODY {"error":"controller_tx_unsupported"}, END

api_request_not_found.summary: a request for an unknown path, id 2
api_request_not_found.outcome: the channel routes only /api/v1/* table entries; the answer is api_response_not_found

api_response_not_found.summary: the 404 for an unknown path, id 2
api_response_not_found.outcome: RES_HEAD 404 with no headers, RES_BODY '404 Not Found', END

api_request_ok.outcome: a request with no body is REQ_HEAD + END; the answer is api_response_ok

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' ws: wss:; img-src 'self' data:; script-src 'self'; media-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net

api_response_ok.outcome: RES_HEAD {status, headers}, one RES_BODY per <= 16 KB of body, then END

api_request_chunked.summary: a request whose answer is chunked, id 4
api_request_chunked.outcome: the answer body exceeds response_chunk_bytes, so the RES_BODY arrives as several messages: see api_response_chunked

api_response_chunked.summary: a chunked multi-message body (> 16 KB), id 4

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self' ws: wss:; img-src 'self' data:; script-src 'self'; media-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net

api_response_chunked.outcome: RES_HEAD, then one RES_BODY per 16384-byte chunk (here 16384 + 1 bytes), then END; the body is the concatenation of the chunks in order

api_error_stale_id.summary: the ERROR for a reused request id, id 5
api_error_stale_id.trigger: send the head of api_request_not_found with id 5 twice: the first is served, the resend answers ERROR stale_id (a rejected head never consumes its id, so it may be retried)

api_error_timeout.summary: the ERROR for a request past the deadline, id 6
api_error_timeout.trigger: a request whose reassembly or dispatch outlasts request_deadline_s answers ERROR timeout and the channel keeps serving

api_error_too_large.summary: the ERROR for an oversized body, id 7
api_error_too_large.trigger: REQ_HEAD id 7 then REQ_BODY frames of 16384 'x' bytes each: the frame that pushes the assembled body past max_request_body_bytes answers ERROR too_large and never dispatches

api_error_busy.summary: the ERROR for the 33rd in-flight request, id 40
api_error_busy.trigger: 33 REQ_HEADs with no END: ids 8..39 are accepted (the 32 in-flight slots); the 33rd head answers ERROR busy

api_error_malformed.summary: the ERROR for a malformed frame, id 0
api_error_malformed.trigger: any binary frame shorter than the 7-byte header (the four bytes 01 02 00 00) or a text frame answers ERROR malformed on id 0 and the channel stays open

api_cancel.summary: CANCEL drops request 41 before it answers
api_cancel.outcome: the server drops request 41: no frame is ever sent for it, and the channel keeps serving

api_unknown_id_ignored.summary: frames for an unknown request id are a no-op, id 9999
api_unknown_id_ignored.outcome: silently ignored: no ERROR, no answer; the channel keeps serving
